Learn moreSign in Comments 2 Top Show featured comments Newest Show recent comments, including potential spam Description The Jones Act Explained 18Likes909ViewsNov 182025 Discover what the Jones Act—also known as the Merchant Marine Act of 1920—actually means for maritime workers. If you’re a commercial fisherman, cargo ship crew member, harbor worker, or fixed-rig employee and you’re injured on navigable waters, you may qualify as a Jones Act Seaman with powerful legal rights. This video explains why injuries at sea fall under admiralty law, how that differs from common law, and why the Jones Act restores your right to a jury trial for personal injury claims. Orlando & Associates breaks down the constitutional protections, what makes a worker a Jones Act Seaman, and what you should do if you’re hurt on the job. If you work on the water, this is information you must know. Subscribe for more insights on maritime law, personal injury cases, and your rights under federal law.
